instructions:
horus makes images on this machine with local AI models. You do not need to know how.
1. Call list_workflows. Each workflow is one image model and graph; pick the one whose summary and good_for fit.
2. Call describe_workflow for that workflow once, and read subject.rules.
   horus adds no style: it sends your subject to the model exactly as written. You own the look,
   the palette, the light and the composition, so write them in the subject.
3. Call generate_image. It waits until the PNG is on disk (often 3 to 8 minutes, longer on a cold start)
   and returns its absolute path. Open the file and check it against what you asked.
Every result has ok, result and error. On ok=false, read error.code, error.action_by and error.next_step:
action_by "retry" = call again, "caller" = change your arguments, "human" = ask the user to do error.next_step.
Never install or uninstall a workflow without the user's consent: those tools ask for it.

tools.title: Describe an image workflow

tools.description: Make one image with the given workflow and save it as a PNG on this machine. The call waits until the image is done (often 3 to 8 minutes; the first call after a cold start takes longer) and reports progress. The subject is the whole prompt: what the picture shows and how it looks (style, palette, light, composition). horus sends it to the model exactly as written and adds nothing. The result has the absolute path of the PNG; open it and check it. The same subject and seed give the same image.

tools.description: Download and verify (SHA-256) the model files of one image workflow, so that generate_image can use it. Files that are already present are kept. Downloads are large (several GB) and can take 10 to 60 minutes. The models have their own license: the first call without accept_license=true returns the error LICENSE_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED with the license and the size. Ask the user, then call again with accept_license=true. The call waits until the install is done and reports progress.

accept_license.description: True only after the user accepted the license shown in the first reply.
